*Saṁkiliṭṭhattika, Kusalattika* (Patthana 17.24) is a canonical Abhidhamma text located in the *Paṭṭhāna* collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Structurally, it treats the combinatorial exposition of the triad on states associated with defilement (*saṁkiliṭṭhattika*) in relation to the triad on wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states (*kusalattika*) [SuttaCentral].
No direct external parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan traditions are recorded [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial textual alignments occur with *Tika Kusalattika* (Patthana 5.2), sharing 10 matches and 2,457 characters (including §1.1–4.1 aligned with §32.1–36.1), and the immediately preceding section, *Upādinnattika, Kusalattika* (Patthana 17.23), which shares 3 matches and 1,530 characters (§0.1–4.1 aligned with §0.1–4.1) [DharmaNexus]. Notable reuse also connects it with reciprocal pairings such as *Kusalattika, Saṁkiliṭṭhattika* (Patthana 17.4 and Patthana 23.4) as well as *Kusalattika, Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 16.25) [DharmaNexus].
